entries_new.name: Kingdom of Talossa
entries_new.mechanism: A founder declared a kingdom from his bedroom, later claiming part of Milwaukee, and kept it going through a web community of citizens.
entries_new.story: Talossa is a micronation (a self-declared country that no state recognises) that Robert Ben Madison founded on 26 December 1979 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, at age 14. At first it covered only his bedroom. It now claims part of Milwaukee, which it calls the Greater Talossan Area, and no state or the United Nations accepts the claim. Madison disestablished the kingdom in 2005, and its citizens kept it going. As of 5 August 2023 it reported 157 active citizens and 564 registered people in total. Madison also invented the Talossan language for it in 1980.

entries_new.name: Antarctic Micronational Union
entries_new.founder: Flandrensis, Mary State and the Kingdom of Finismund
entries_new.mechanism: Micronations that claim Antarctic ground sign treaties among themselves to recognise each other's claims.
entries_new.story: The Antarctic Micronational Union (AMU) is an organisation of micronations, which are self-declared countries that no state recognises, formed to regulate micronational claims in Antarctica. It was founded on 6 December 2008 by the Grand Duchy of Flandrensis, Mary State and the Kingdom of Finismund to settle a conflict with the Grand Duchy of Westarctica. Westarctica signed the West Antarctic Treaty and joined on 24 September 2010. The AMU was dissolved in 2016, when nine micronations signed a new treaty, and was revived on 24 February 2020. Its stated purpose is to protect members' claims against other claimants.
entries_new.anchor: Marie Byrd Land, Antarctica (the sector at the centre of the 2008 dispute)

entries_new.name: Organisation de la microfrancophonie
entries_new.story: The Organisation de la microfrancophonie (Microfrancophonie) is a body of French-speaking micronations, which are self-declared countries that no state recognises. It is modelled on the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie. Wikipedia gives its founding as 2015 in the article and 2016 in the list of micronations. It had 27 member states and one observer as of August 2024. Four summits have been held: Aigues-Mortes (September 2016), Vincennes (July 2018), Blaye (August 2022) and Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye (August 2024), where 35 delegates represented 13 members and five non-members.
entries_new.anchor: Aigues-Mortes, France (site of the first summit)

entries_new.name: Republic of Rathnelly
entries_new.passports: Issued to everyone in the neighbourhood
entries_new.challenge: City plans for an expressway; zoning of a park for city workers
entries_new.mechanism: A neighbourhood declared itself a republic during a national celebration, as a protest and a street party.
entries_new.story: Rathnelly is the south-eastern section of the South Hill neighbourhood in Toronto, Ontario. On 1 July 1967, during Canada's Centennial celebrations, it declared itself an independent republic. Wikipedia links the unrest to city plans for an expressway through the area and to a local park being zoned for city workers only. The republic elected a queen, held a parade, formed an air force of 1,000 helium balloons and issued passports to everyone in the neighbourhood. It still holds a street party in June every second year, called Rathnelly Day.

entries_new.name: Thylejren
entries_new.mechanism: A festival campsite turned into a lasting alternative settlement inside Denmark.
entries_new.story: Thylejren (Thy Camp, also called Frøstruplejren) began as a festival in summer 1970, organised by the community Det Ny Samfund (The New Society). It was held in Han Herred, between Frøstrup and Østerild near Thy in north-western Denmark, and was inspired by the Isle of Wight Festival and Woodstock. Some participants stayed through the winter, and the camp became a permanent settlement of homemade houses. Wikipedia reports a population of 65 as of 2020 and calls it a micronation with its own territory, within Danish society.

entries_new.name: Free Republic of Wackerland
entries_new.pop: About 400 at the start; over 150 huts and tents
entries_new.challenge: Bavarian police and Federal Border Guards
entries_new.mechanism: Protesters occupied a nuclear plant construction site and declared it a republic to block clearing of the forest.
entries_new.story: The Free Republic of Wackerland was a hut village built by protesters in the Taxölden Forest near Bodenwöhr, Bavaria, on the construction site of the Wackersdorf nuclear fuel reprocessing plant. After clearing work was paused on 21 December 1985, about 400 opponents of the plant reoccupied the site and built over 150 huts and tents. The name copies the Free Republic of Wendland of 1980. On 7 January 1986 about 2,000 police cleared it, and over 1,000 people, mostly from out of town, were held for identification. Several protesters were injured, some by police dogs.

entries_new.name: Republic of Kinney
entries_new.founder: Mayor Mary P. Anderson and the Kinney city council
entries_new.passports: Over 1,600 sold at $1 each, March to April 1978
entries_new.recognition: Duluth businessman Jeno Paulucci offered the first 'foreign aid' on 13 February 1978; the United States never acknowledged the secession
entries_new.cost: $186,000 estimated for the water system; $198,000 grant approved in November 1978
entries_new.mechanism: A town announced its secession from the United States by letter to the Secretary of State to draw attention to a funding problem.
entries_new.story: Kinney is a city in St. Louis County, Minnesota. In 1977 its water system was failing and replacement was priced at $186,000, and applications to state and federal agencies had failed. Mayor Mary Anderson and the council sent a secession letter to US Secretary of State Cyrus Vance on 13 July 1977, expecting that foreign aid would follow a secession and an immediate lost war. The story reached national news in February 1978. In November 1978 a regional board approved a $198,000 grant for the water system. The republic sold over 1,600 passports at $1 each in March and April 1978.

entries_new.name: State of Scott
entries_new.stopped_by: Repealed by the county itself in 1986
entries_new.mechanism: A county court voted to leave the state that had left the Union.
entries_new.story: Scott County, Tennessee, voted 541 to 19 against Tennessee's secession from the Union on 8 June 1861. Later that year its county court passed a resolution declaring the county the Free and Independent State of Scott. Governor Isham Harris sent about 1,700 soldiers toward Huntsville, and Wikipedia says they retreated before reaching the town. Neither the Union nor the Confederacy recognised the declaration. A minor fight, the Battle of Huntsville, took place on 13 August 1862. The county repealed its secession in 1986 and was ceremonially readmitted to Tennessee, though the state had never accepted the secession.

entries_new.name: Embassy of Heaven
entries_new.stopped_by: Property seized for non-payment of taxes in 1997
entries_new.challenge: Sheriff's deputies, federal authorities (who assert the group exists to avoid taxes), Minnesota insurance regulators in 2012
entries_new.mechanism: A church declares its members citizens of a heavenly kingdom and issues its own documents.
entries_new.story: The Embassy of Heaven is a Christian religious group based in Stayton, Oregon. Its members say they are citizens of the Kingdom of Heaven and reject what they call worldly governments. It issues its own identity documents, licences and plates. Its leader, Craig Douglas Fleshman, uses the name Pastor Paul Revere. In 1997 sheriff's deputies raided and seized the property for unpaid taxes, which the leader said were not owed because it was a separate nation. The Anti-Defamation League classes the group with the sovereign citizen movement. Glen Stoll, linked to it, pleaded guilty in 2021 to conspiracy to defraud the United States and tax evasion.

entries_new.name: Freistaat Odonien
entries_new.mechanism: An artist turned a rented plot into a self-named free state used as a studio and event site.
entries_new.story: Freistaat Odonien (Free State of Odonia) is an open studio and arts site in the Neuehrenfeld district of Cologne, Germany. In 2005 the sculptor Odo Rumpf converted a vacant 5,000 square metre plot between railway tracks near the Cologne goods depot. Other artists use the site, which has metal sculptures and hosts exhibitions, festivals, music, film and dance events, and a beer garden that can be rented. It holds a twice-yearly robot show called Robodonien. Wikipedia lists it among micronations in Germany.

entries_new.name: Dusit Thani
entries_new.laws: A constitution written by the king, used only inside the model city
entries_new.mechanism: A king ran a model city with its own elections and constitution to teach democratic practice.
entries_new.story: Dusit Thani (town in heaven) was a miniature city that King Vajiravudh (Rama VI) of Siam built in the 1910s and 1920s as a model of democracy. It stood on about one acre, first in Dusit Park and, from the end of 1919, at Phaya Thai, with buildings at one fifteenth of life size. Members of the court registered and bought land to become citizens. Elections were held between a Blue and a Red party, a constitution written by the king was applied, and two newspapers were published. The constitution applied only in the model. The project stopped when the king died in 1925.

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Pineal
entries_new.stopped_by: Withdrawal of most members after the controversies, per Wikipedia
entries_new.pop: About 100 at the peak; four reported in late 2023
entries_new.challenge: Public Prosecution Service, Oliveira do Hospital municipality
entries_new.mechanism: A spiritual community on a bought plot proclaimed itself a sovereign kingdom.
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Pineal is a self-proclaimed kingdom in Oliveira do Hospital, central Portugal. Wikipedia says that around 2019 or 2020 Água Akbal Pinheiro (born Martin Junior Kenny in Zimbabwe) and his wife settled there with about forty people from eight countries, on land bought by a footballer. Portuguese authorities do not recognise it and it is legally a private company. Prosecutors opened an investigation in 2023 into the death of a child in the community, and the municipality asked for child-protection and border-service checks. The article reports that by late 2023 only the founder, his partner and two children remained.

entries_new.name: Lauwiner Empire
entries_new.challenge: Officials in canton Lucerne objected to road tolls
entries_new.mechanism: Buying or claiming ownerless land plots across Switzerland and treating them as the empire's territory.
entries_new.story: The Lauwiner Empire is a symbolic realm founded by Jonas Lauwiner, a Swiss politician and landowner. He gained ownerless plots through usucaption (acquiring title by long use) after finding them marked as ownerless in the land register. He held a coronation in Bern in 2019 and keeps a palace in a former paint factory in Oberburg. The empire does not claim independence from Switzerland. As of 2025 he owned 149 plots and 83 roads, 114,000 square metres across nine cantons. He charges tolls on some roads, and in 2025 officials in canton Lucerne asked their government to find a solution.

entries_new.name: Morokulien
entries_new.founder: Swedish and Norwegian peace movements (monument); a 1959 radio broadcast (the microstate)
entries_new.mechanism: A peace park on a border is declared a ceremonial microstate through a joint radio broadcast.
entries_new.story: Morokulien, also called Fredsriket (The Republic of Peace), is a 6-hectare symbolic area on the Norway-Sweden border, between Magnor and Eda glasbruk. A peace monument was inaugurated there on 16 August 1914 to mark a century of peace between the two countries, with about 12,000 people attending. In 1959, during a joint Swedish-Norwegian radio broadcast, the site became the ceremonial microstate of Morokulien. It lies inside the demilitarised border zone set by the Karlstad Convention of 1905. In 2025 a police station jointly staffed by Norwegian and Swedish officers opened there.

entries_new.name: Veyshnoria
entries_new.challenge: Lida District Court (2022); Belarus Ministry of Internal Affairs (2026)
entries_new.mechanism: Online users adopted a military exercise's fictional enemy state as a joke nation with sign-up citizenship.
entries_new.story: Veyshnoria is a fictional state invented as an enemy for Zapad 2017, a joint Russian-Belarusian military exercise held on 14 to 20 September 2017, and mapped over most of Belarus's Grodno Region. Internet users turned it into a joke state, starting with a satirical Twitter account on 30 August 2017. A web-based Veyshnoria later collected over 18,000 sign-ups for citizenship, and the Taler cryptocurrency became its official currency. In August 2022 a court in Lida declared its social networks extremist materials, and in 2026 the Belarusian Ministry of Internal Affairs declared Veyshnoria an extremist group.

entries_new.name: Kailaasa
entries_new.passports: Claims to issue passports and visas
entries_new.challenge: Arrest warrant in India; UN ignored its submission
entries_new.mechanism: A religious leader proclaimed a nation of NGOs and followers and sought recognition through local and national governments.
entries_new.story: Kailaasa (United States of Kailaasa) is a self-declared nation announced in December 2019 by Nithyananda, an Indian spiritual leader who is the subject of an Indian arrest warrant relating to rape allegations, which he denies. Representatives describe it as a borderless, service-oriented nation run through NGOs, while India Today reported an island near Ecuador. It announced a Reserve Bank and gold coins in 2020. No government recognises it. Its representatives have sought sister-city agreements and UN recognition, and in November 2023 a Paraguayan ministry official was replaced after signing an agreement with them.
entries_new.anchor: Bidadi, Karnataka (founder's original ashram; no confirmed territory)

entries_new.name: Principality of Piddington
entries_new.mechanism: A village voted symbolically to leave the United Kingdom in protest at a local housing decision.
entries_new.story: Piddington is a village about 4.5 miles south-east of Bicester in Oxfordshire, England, with 358 residents at the 2021 census. In September 2026 residents voted in a symbolic referendum in favour of leaving the United Kingdom. The vote responded to the government's plan to house 1,250 asylum seekers at nearby MOD Bicester, a former military base. Wikipedia lists the village among micronations in England. The article gives no vote count and no claim of legal independence, and no state recognises it.

entries_new.name: Republic of Lamb
entries_new.cost: £30,000 (the 2009 purchase of Lamb and the two Dog islands)
entries_new.mechanism: The owner of a small bought island declared it a republic with an anthem and a national football team.
entries_new.story: Lamb is an uninhabited island about 100 by 50 metres in the Firth of Forth, off North Berwick in Scotland. It was part of the feudal barony of Dirleton and was sold in 2009 for £30,000 to Uri Geller, who has said he believes it hides ancient Egyptian treasure. In mid-2022 Geller sought to declare it the Republic of Lamb, a micronation with its own national anthem. He also became chairman of North Berwick Amateurs FC, which he designated Lamb's national football team.

entries_new.name: Pictish Free State
entries_new.challenge: HM Government, over diplomatic plates and non-compliance with UK law
entries_new.mechanism: A land owner declared a free state for a historic culture and expanded it through donated acreage.
entries_new.story: The Pictish Free State was set up in 1977 by Robbie the Pict (Brian Robertson, born 1945) to raise awareness of Pictish culture. It began with one acre of his own land on the Isle of Skye and grew to over 1,000 acres through supporters' donations. Operating through a body called the Pictish High Commission, Robertson has been in conflict with the UK government over his use of Pictish diplomatic registration plates and his non-compliance with UK laws. He also campaigned against the Skye Bridge toll, which was abolished in 2004.

entries_new.name: Aristasia
entries_new.founder: Marianne Martindale was its prominent face
entries_new.mechanism: A subculture treated an imagined country as a place to live in, with an embassy and its own geography.
entries_new.story: Aristasia was a British female-focused subcultural group and shared role-playing world that combined Guénonian Traditionalism with lesbian separatism. It began in the Oxford area in the 1960s or 1970s and drew most media attention in the 1990s. Members re-created the lifestyles of the 1920s to 1950s. Eras became places in an imagined geography, and no men existed in it. Estimates of size ranged from dozens to hundreds. It kept an Aristasian Embassy in a private London house and moved to websites and Second Life from the mid-1990s. Wikipedia lists it among micronations in the United Kingdom.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Category: Micronations in the United Kingdom

entries_new.name: Mini-dokuritsukoku (Japan's micronation boom)
entries_new.mechanism: Towns and businesses declared humorous independent countries as a tourism and local-identity campaign.
entries_new.story: Mini-dokuritsukoku (mini independent countries) are micronations, meaning self-declared countries that no state recognises, founded in Japan mainly in the 1980s. Local communities and businesses such as inns declared independence to promote tourism and local culture and to slow the movement of young people to cities. By 1988 about 150 existed, and about 203 were founded during the boom, with a smaller second wave in 1988 and 1989 when the government announced the 100 Million Yen Project for municipalities. Most were light-hearted and did not seek to leave Japan. Fewer than 50 remained in 2016, and a 2020 study counted 40 active.

entries_new.name: Republic of Ōshima (1946)
entries_new.stopped_by: Return of the island to Japanese administration on 22 March
entries_new.mechanism: Islanders drafted a charter for a republic after an administrative oversight left the island outside Japanese rule.
entries_new.story: After the Second World War the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers removed Izu Ōshima, an island south of Tokyo, from Japanese administration in 1946 through an oversight. Realising the mistake, islanders drafted the Ōshima Charter, which called for a Republic of Ōshima. The island was restored to Japanese rule on 22 March, ending 53 days of autonomy. Wikipedia counts it among micronations created inadvertently during the Occupation of Japan.

entries_new.name: Bonin Islands under US Navy rule
entries_new.stopped_by: End of US Navy governance in 1968
entries_new.passports: ID cards listing Chichi-jima as nationality
entries_new.mechanism: Residents formed a council and used island-based ID cards while the islands sat under US Navy governance.
entries_new.story: Between 1946 and 1968 the Bonin Islands were governed by the United States Navy and were made part of neither the United States nor Japan. Native islanders set up a Bonin Islands Council and travelled with ID cards that listed Chichi-jima, the main island, as their nationality. Wikipedia counts this among micronations created inadvertently during the Occupation of Japan.

entries_new.name: New Yamatai State
entries_new.mechanism: A city declared a micronation named after a legendary ancient state to revive its economy.
entries_new.story: The New Yamatai State was founded in 1977 by residents of Usa, Ōita Prefecture, Japan, and named after the legendary Yamatai state. It aimed to revive the city's economy. Wikipedia lists it among the micronations of Japan. Its activities were suspended in 2010 and restarted in 2020 in response to the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.

entries_new.name: Kirikiri Country
entries_new.mechanism: A town adopted the fictional country of a novel and held mock UN-style summits.
entries_new.story: Kirikiri Country in Ōtsuchi, Iwate Prefecture, is named after Kirikirijin, a 1981 novel by Hisashi Inoue about a village that secedes from Japan and makes its marginalised dialect the national language. Wikipedia says the story was in turn inspired by the micronation of New Atlantis. The real-life Kirikiri Country hosted its own version of United Nations summits between 1983 and 1985. The article gives no later history for it.

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Inobhutan
entries_new.recognition: A friendship treaty signed by a Japanese ministry figure; the Foreign Ministry disagreed
entries_new.mechanism: A town declared a kingdom whose name plays on Bhutan and obtained a symbolic friendship treaty.
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Inobhutan is a Japanese micronation based in Susami, Wakayama Prefecture. Wikipedia reports that Michio Watanabe of the Ministry of International Trade and Industry signed a friendship treaty between Japan and the kingdom as a publicity stunt. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disagreed with it, fearing it might offend the real Kingdom of Bhutan, whose name sounds similar. The article gives no founding date.

entries_new.name: Nikoniko Republic
entries_new.mechanism: A town declared a republic with its own time zone and coins for local promotion.
entries_new.story: The Nikoniko Republic, in Nihonmatsu, Fukushima Prefecture, is one of the micronations of Japan's 1980s boom. Wikipedia says it established its own time zone and minted its own currency. Wikipedia estimates that about 203 micronations were founded in Japan during the boom, most as light-hearted ventures that did not seek to leave Japan. The article gives no founding date or end date for this one.

entries_new.name: Alcohol Republic
entries_new.mechanism: A local group declared a micronation and sent its president as a delegate of micronations to the Vatican.
entries_new.story: The Alcohol Republic is a micronation on Sado Island, Niigata Prefecture, Japan, listed among the micronations of the 1980s boom. In 1987 its president, representing a peace delegation of micronations, visited Vatican City and shook hands with Pope John Paul II. Wikipedia estimates that about 203 micronations were founded in Japan during the boom, mostly for publicity and tourism. It gives no founding date for this one.

entries_new.name: Gin'nan Federation and the Mini-dokuritsukoku Olympics
entries_new.mechanism: One micronation hosted a television event that gathered others, in place of any shared territory.
entries_new.story: In 1986 the Gin'nan Federation, a Japanese micronation, hosted a micronation version of the Olympic Games, the Mini-dokuritsukoku Olympics, which was broadcast on prime-time television. Wikipedia describes most such micronations as publicity ventures that did not challenge Japanese sovereignty.
entries_new.anchor: Japan (location of the federation not stated)

entries_new.name: Other named Japanese micronations
entries_new.mechanism: Local tourism and identity micronations listed together without individual detail.
entries_new.story: Wikipedia's article on Japanese micronations also names these, each with its place: Akhotsk Republic (Bihoro, Hokkaido), Crab Kingdom (Hyōgo), Commonwealth of Cassiopeia (Iwate), Country of Nature (Saikai, Nagasaki), Drift Ice Iceland Republic (Monbetsu), Frog Village (Daisen, Akita), Galactic Federation (JAXA sites), Ginko Federation (Hachiōji), Kakuda, Noshiro, Sagamihara, Saku, Taiki, Sanrikuofunato and Uchinourakimotsuki republics, Panauru Kingdom (Yoron), Potato Republic (Niseko), Shiso Forest Kingdom, Soyankda United States (Osaka) and Tsuchinoko Republic (Nara). No dates are given.

entries_new.name: Naminara Republic
entries_new.mechanism: A tourist island resort presents itself as a country for visitors.
entries_new.story: The Naminara Republic is a self-declared micronation on Nami Island (Namiseom) in Chuncheon, Gangwon Province, South Korea. The island was formed when the Bukhan River rose after the Cheongpyeong Dam was built in 1944, and Min Byeong-do bought it in 1965. A tourism company developed it as a resort from 1966. Wikipedia describes the republic as a tourist destination that advocates the concept of a nation. It gives no founding date.

entries_new.name: MicroCon
entries_new.mechanism: Micronations meet in rented public venues to exchange ideas.
entries_new.story: MicroCon is a convention of micronationalists held every second year since 11 April 2015, created by Kevin Baugh of the Republic of Molossia. The first was at the Anaheim Central Library in California. Each later edition has been hosted by a different micronation, among them Tucker, Georgia (2017, over 70 delegates from 26 micronations), Hamilton, Ontario (2019, 113 attendees from 43 micronations) and Las Vegas (2022, 100 attendees from 30). The 2023 edition split into a summit in Joliet, Illinois and one in Ypres, Belgium.

entries_new.name: PoliNation
entries_new.founder: Judy Lattas, George Cruickshank and Princess Paula
entries_new.mechanism: Micronations and researchers hold conferences on micronational topics.
entries_new.story: PoliNation is a conference of micronationalists, held sporadically since 17 April 2010 and attended by academics, authors and journalists. The first took place on Dangar Island, Sydney, organised by Judy Lattas of Macquarie University, George Cruickshank of the Empire of Atlantium and Princess Paula of the Principality of Snake Hill. Later editions were in London on 14 July 2012 and in the Free Republic of Alcatraz near Perugia, Italy, on 4 and 5 July 2015, with 14 micronations registered. A 2024 event planned in Australia was cancelled for lack of interest.

entries_new.name: Joseon Cybernation
entries_new.founder: Andrew Lee (claimant to the headship of the House of Yi)
entries_new.recognition: Reported by Wikipedia: Antigua and Barbuda, 2023 (not confirmed from a second source)
entries_new.mechanism: A digital monarchy asserts continuity with a historical Korean kingdom and seeks recognition from small states.
entries_new.story: The Joseon Cybernation is a digital, crypto-backed monarchy with no territory, established in 2022. It claims to be the historical Kingdom of Joseon and Korean Empire, based on Andrew Lee's claim to be head of the House of Yi. Wikipedia's article on micronations states that in 2023 Antigua and Barbuda officially recognised it. Only that one article was read, so the recognition is stated as reported there and not confirmed from a second source.
entries_new.anchor: Seoul (the historical seat of Joseon; the entity has no territory)

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Ruritania (micronation)
entries_new.founder: Queen Anastasia von Rubenroth (ruler named as host)
entries_new.mechanism: A fictional country from a novel is adopted as the basis of a hobby micronation.
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Ruritania is a micronation based in Atlanta, Georgia, modelled on the fictional country of Ruritania from Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda. Wikipedia places it among micronations whose claims are cultural more than territorial. Its ruler, Queen Anastasia von Rubenroth, hosted MicroCon 2017 on 23 to 25 June in Tucker, Georgia, which more than 70 delegates from 26 micronations attended. No founding date is given.

entries_new.name: Kingdom of Slabovia / United Slabovian Empire
entries_new.mechanism: A hobby micronation hosts the biennial micronation convention.
entries_new.story: The Kingdom of Slabovia, called the United Slabovian Empire in Wikipedia's MicroCon article, is a micronation that hosted MicroCon 2019 on 19 to 21 July in Hamilton, Ontario. The event included a gala dinner and a laser tag tournament and drew 113 attendees from 43 micronations, the largest edition. The two articles give it different names, and neither gives a founding date or founder.

entries_new.name: Empire of Angyalistan
entries_new.mechanism: A protest micronation claims floating waste areas of the ocean to draw attention to them.
entries_new.story: The Empire of Angyalistan is a micronation that claims the garbage patches of the world's oceans, in protest against their existence. It hosted the second summit of the Organisation de la microfrancophonie in Vincennes, Paris, on 21 July 2018, attended by fifteen people, with an exhibition of micronational passports, currencies and newspapers at a local museum. No founding date or founder is given in the sources read.

entries_new.name: Aynvaul
entries_new.mechanism: A cultural revival group presents itself as a micronation without a defined territory.
entries_new.story: Aynvaul is described by Wikipedia as what appears to be an Irish-American and Irish-language revival micronation based in or around Long Island, New York. It is one of the micronations whose claims are cultural more than territorial.

entries_new.name: Free Republic of Alcatraz
entries_new.mechanism: A micronation hosts a conference and issues a climate treaty among micronations.
entries_new.story: The Free Republic of Alcatraz is a micronation near Perugia in Umbria, Italy. It hosted PoliNation 2015, a conference of micronationalists held on 4 and 5 July, at which 14 micronations had registered to attend. Topics included an intermicronational organisation similar to the United Nations, trade between micronations and the Alcatraz Environmental Treaty of 2015 on climate change, which was unveiled there. No founding date or founder is given.

entries_new.name: Principality of Hélianthis
entries_new.mechanism: A micronation hosts the intermicronational summit of its member group.
entries_new.story: The Principality of Hélianthis is a French-speaking micronation that organised the third summit of the Organisation de la microfrancophonie in Blaye, Nouvelle-Aquitaine, on 27 and 28 August 2022. Fifteen people attended, representing seven member states.

entries_new.name: Formori Community
entries_new.mechanism: A micronation community hosts the group's summit in a village.
entries_new.story: The Formori Community is a member of the Organisation de la microfrancophonie that hosted its fourth summit at Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye in Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes on 24 and 25 August 2024. Thirty-five delegates attended, representing thirteen member states and five non-members.

entries_new.name: League of Secessionist States
entries_new.founder: Robert Ben Madison and two friends
entries_new.mechanism: Micronations joined a club to recognise one another and share news, replacing any shared territory.
entries_new.story: The League of Secessionist States was an organisation of micronations first founded in 1980 by Talossa's founder Robert Ben Madison and two friends. Madison re-established it in April 1996, when the dormant league got a website. From 1997 to at least 2000 it was the most prominent intermicronational organisation on the Internet. The article does not give the league's end date.
